results.claim: Reachability is exactly a sparse unary congruence-closure query.
results.proof_sketch: Write each dual edge as (o,X,t) and reverse it into a labeled transition t→_X o. An equivalence R induces a label-functional quotient transition relation exactly when, for every (o,X,t),(o',X,t'), t R t' implies o R o': transitions with the same label from one quotient state must have one quotient destination. Thus the finest such quotient is the least stable equivalence θ, equivalently the unary congruence generated by equations f_X(t)=o. This is precisely the source's wormhole relation: matched enter/exit paths preserve the stack and yield θ-equalities, while every generating fold is realized by entering the common box, traversing between equivalent targets, and exiting. Therefore the maze is exitable exactly when the starting wire and some outer-pin wire have the same image in this quotient. Pin identifiers distinguish source edges but do not alter θ.

results.claim: The congruence closure and exit query decompose exactly over weak components of the undirected support graph.
results.proof_sketch: Let H have the wires as vertices and an undirected edge {t,o} for every dual edge (o,X,t). The relation S of belonging to the same component of H is stable: if t S t' and (o,X,t),(o',X,t') are edges, then t,o,t',o' all lie in one H-component, so o S o'. Since θ is the least stable equivalence, θ⊆S; no closure equality crosses components. For each component C, compute its least closure θ_C using only edges in C. The disjoint union of the θ_C is stable globally, while the restriction of global θ to C is a stable relation containing the local generators. Minimality in both directions therefore gives θ restricted to C equal to θ_C. Hence only the component containing the starting wire can contain an equivalent accepting wire. H and that component are found in O(W+E) time. This is an exact reduction, although a worst-case instance may have one component.

results.claim: There is a deterministic O(W+B+E α(W+E)+E log(min{B,E}+1))-time, O(W+E+B)-space algorithm, sharpening the general sparse bound and eliminating dense W·B initialization.
results.proof_sketch:
Maintain a disjoint-set union (DSU) of wire classes and, for each current root C, a finite map D_C keyed by boxes; D_C[X] retains one original edge (o,X,t) with t in C. Radix-sort initial edges by (t,X), retain one per group, and queue an origin pair for every discarded duplicate. When a queued pair has distinct DSU roots, union them and meld their maps. A common key X queues the two retained origins and discards one entry. DSU-root selection and map-meld orientation are independent.

Every queued equality is forced when created. Each queue insertion discards a distinct original edge, so there are at most E insertions. At quiescence, same-X edges whose targets share a class have met in that class's map, so their origins share a class. Soundness and terminal stability prove that the result is θ.

The O(E) DSU operations cost O(Eα(W+E)). Let K=min{B,E}. A deterministic split/join balanced-tree meld of sizes m≤n costs O(m log(n/m+1)). With φ(0)=0 and φ(q)=q log q, its cost is bounded by the disjoint-union potential increase. If d duplicate keys are deleted, replacing the hypothetical size m+n by the actual size loses only O(d log(K+1)). Actual potential changes telescope to O(E log(K+1)), and at most E entries are deleted. Initial radix grouping costs O(W+E+B), and all structures use O(W+E+B) space.

results.claim: Both outcomes have certificates of size O(W+E) verifiable deterministically in O(W+E+B) time.
results.proof_sketch:
For a negative certificate, supply a class number P(v) for every wire. Radix-sort edges (o,X,t) by (X,P(t)) and verify that every group has one value P(o). This makes P a stable congruence. Since θ refines every stable congruence, separating the start from every outer-pin wire proves nonreachability; θ itself supplies a certificate for every negative instance.

For a positive certificate, supply a chronological binary merge forest with at most W−1 internal nodes. Each internal node identifies two earlier child components, two original same-box edges, and an earlier node q containing both targets. Verify edge identities and boxes, that the origins lie in the two child subtrees, and that the targets lie below q. DFS intervals give constant-time containment tests. Inductively q proves the targets already equivalent, so the folding rule justifies the merge. A root containing the start and an outer-pin wire proves exit. Recording the successful unions of any folding computation supplies such a forest, including a leaf q when the two targets coincide.

results.claim: The target O(W+E+B) bound holds for graded dual graphs: graphs admitting an integer rank ρ with ρ(o)=ρ(t)+1 for every edge (o,X,t).
results.proof_sketch:
Generated equivalences never cross ranks. Process ranks increasingly. Once rank r−1 is final, group every edge whose origin has rank r by (X,class(t)); connect each group's origins by a star and compute ordinary connected components among rank-r wires. These are exactly the final rank-r classes: all required merges use equivalent rank-(r−1) targets, and higher ranks cannot later affect rank r.

Grouping avoids a W·B table. Bucket a rank's edges by X using a B-entry timestamp array, then use a W-entry timestamp array keyed by target-class identifiers within each touched X bucket. Every edge and wire receives O(1) aggregate work, giving O(W+E+B) time and space. If ρ is absent, DFS assigns and checks the difference constraints in each weak component in O(W+E) time; componentwise normalization puts all ranks in an O(W)-sized range.

results.claim: On W-wire graded dual graphs, the exact maximum number of changing synchronous fixed-point rounds is floor((W−1)/2); this is attained with one box and E=2 floor((W−1)/2).
results.proof_sketch:
Let P₀ be equality, and let each round equivalence-close Pᵢ together with every origin equality whose same-box targets are Pᵢ-equivalent. If round k changes the partition, some newly enabled generator joins two previous classes. For k>1 its distinct targets became equivalent in round k−1. Recursively tracing such a newly enabling equality reaches a round-one generator with an identical target. Grading places the resulting nontrivial equalities at k distinct consecutive ranks, requiring two wires per equality rank and one bottom target. Hence W≥2k+1 and k≤floor((W−1)/2).

For equality, let R=floor((W−1)/2). Use z and pairs a₀,b₀,…,a_{R−1},b_{R−1}, plus an isolated wire when W is even. With one box X, add a₀→X z and b₀→X z and, for 1≤j<R, add aⱼ→X a_{j−1} and bⱼ→X b_{j−1}. Assign z rank 0 and each aⱼ,bⱼ rank j+1. Round j+1 merges exactly aⱼ,bⱼ. This also covers W=1,2 with zero edges and zero changing rounds.

results.claim: For unrestricted W-wire dual graphs, the universal maximum W−1 changing synchronous rounds is attained with one box, exactly E=W, origin outdegree one, and target indegree at most two.
results.proof_sketch: Every changing round strictly reduces the number of equivalence classes, so at most W−1 occur. For W≥2, use wires v₀,…,v_{W−1}, one box X, and edges (v₀,X,v₀), (v₁,X,v₀), and (vᵢ,X,v_{i−1}) for 2≤i<W. Initially only the first two edges collide, merging v₀,v₁. Inductively, after round r the only nonsingleton class is {v₀,…,vᵣ}; at the next snapshot, exactly v_{r+1} is newly joined. Thus there are W−1 changing rounds. Every wire is one edge's origin, and target indegree is at most two. For W=1, a single self-loop has E=W and zero changing rounds. Distinct pins realize the edges in the source model. Therefore global rescanning of all E edges per round can take Θ(WE)=Θ(W²), but this is only a lower bound for that strategy.

results.claim: The exact minimum number of edges among W-wire instances attaining W−1 changing synchronous rounds is 0 when W=1 and W when W≥2.
results.proof_sketch: For W=1, equality already has one class, so an edgeless instance attains W−1=0 rounds; nonnegativity makes zero minimal. Now assume W≥2. Attaining W−1 changing rounds forces the partition, initially W singleton classes, eventually to have one class: every changing round removes at least one class, and no changes are possible after reaching one. A wire that is not the origin of any edge cannot occur in any nonreflexive pair generated by the closure rule, whose endpoints are always edge origins. It therefore remains singleton forever, contradicting the universal final class. Every wire must consequently occur as an edge origin, so E≥W. The preceding one-box construction has exactly one edge from each wire and attains W−1 rounds, proving equality. This repairs the audit's W=1 counterexample without weakening the W≥2 theorem.

final_writeup:
The claimed resolution remains PARTIAL: I did not obtain the requested unrestricted O(W+E+B)-time algorithm.

The structural lens gives an exact intermediate formulation. Reverse every dual edge (o,X,t) to a labeled transition t→_X o. The desired relation is the finest state quotient on which transitions of each label are functional: whenever equivalent source states have X-transitions, their destinations must be equivalent. This condition is exactly the source's folding rule, so the quotient kernel is the wormhole equivalence, and exit reachability transfers to equality between the quotient images of the starting wire and an outer-pin wire.

This quotient decomposes over weak components of the undirected edge-support graph. The same-component relation is itself stable under every fold, so no generated equality crosses components; conversely, the disjoint union of the closures computed inside the components is globally stable. The exit query may therefore be restricted, after linear preprocessing, to the starting component. This is a genuine reduction but does not improve the worst case, because all input wires and edges may lie in one component.

For unrestricted instances, the verified deterministic bound remains

O(W+B+Eα(W+E)+E log(min{B,E}+1))

with O(W+E+B) space. Sparse per-class box maps eliminate dense W·B initialization. Each collision deletes a distinct retained edge and queues a forced origin equality, giving at most E events; DSU accounts for the inverse-Ackermann term, and deterministic balanced-tree melding accounts for the logarithmic term. The reformulation did not supply a valid way to eliminate both terms.

Both answers nevertheless have O(W+E)-size certificates with deterministic O(W+E+B)-time verification: stable class labelings certify no-instances, and chronological merge forests certify yes-instances. Graded dual graphs admit an actual O(W+E+B)-time increasing-rank algorithm.

The synchronous-round bounds remain useful strategy obstructions. Graded instances have exactly floor((W−1)/2) worst-case changing rounds. Unrestricted instances can attain the universal W−1 bound with one box, E=W, origin outdegree one, and target indegree at most two, so repeated full rescanning can require Θ(W²). The audit's sole refutation is repaired precisely: E=W is edge-minimal for this extremal round count only when W≥2. At W=1, the exact minimum is E=0 because the initial partition is already final.

These round bounds are not computational lower bounds against every algorithm. The structural quotient and component reduction therefore preserve material partial progress but neither prove nor refute the unrestricted source-linear target.
